sights.n: Làng Nổi Tân Lập (Tân Lập Floating Village)
sights.address: Xã Tân Lập, huyện Mộc Hóa, Long An, Vietnam
sights.w: A flooded Melaleuca (tràm) forest reserve ~100 km from Saigon and the marquee nature stop in Long An. A metre-wide concrete path winds ~5 km straight through the cajuput canopy over the water, with a 38 m, 10-storey observation tower over the Đồng Tháp Mười wetlands; explore by rowboat among lotus, water lilies and wild rice. Flood season (roughly Aug–Nov) is peak.

sights.n: Chợ Nổi Cái Bè (Cái Bè Floating Market) — CLOSED
sights.address: Thị trấn Cái Bè, huyện Cái Bè, Tiền Giang, Vietnam
sights.w: One of the Mekong Delta's great floating markets, trading on the Tiền River since the 17th–18th centuries and, by the 19th, a major wholesale hub for rice, dried fish and fruit — each boat hanging its wares from a 'cây bẹo' pole. It sits at the junction of Tiền Giang, Vĩnh Long and Đồng Tháp; go at dawn, and note it has thinned in recent years as road transport rose.

sights.n: Cồn Phụng & the Đạo Dừa Relic (Phoenix Islet)
sights.address: Xã Tân Thạch, huyện Châu Thành, Bến Tre, Vietnam
sights.w: A Tiền-River islet — one of the delta's 'four sacred islets' (Long–Lân–Quy–Phụng) — that is Bến Tre's classic day-trip: coconut-candy workshops, honey-tea gardens, horse-cart rides and boat runs through coconut-palm creeks. At its heart is the surreal relic of the 'Coconut Religion' (Đạo Dừa) founded by France-trained engineer-monk Nguyễn Thành Nam in 1963, with a nine-dragon plaza and octagonal Cửu Trùng Đài tower.

sights.n: Nhà Cổ Huỳnh Thủy Lê (Huỳnh Thủy Lê Ancient House)
sights.address: 255A Nguyễn Huệ, Phường 2, TP. Sa Đéc, Đồng Tháp, Vietnam
sights.w: An 1895 merchant house — French shell, Chinese-Vietnamese interior — that belonged to Huỳnh Thủy Lê, the wealthy young Chinese man whose teenage affair with Marguerite Duras became her Goncourt-winning novel 'The Lover' (L'Amant), filmed by Jean-Jacques Annaud in 1992. A national relic and Sa Đéc's most-visited sight; you can even stay overnight.

sights.n: Làng Hoa Sa Đéc (Sa Đéc Flower Village, Tân Quy Đông)
sights.address: Phường Tân Quy Đông, TP. Sa Đéc, Đồng Tháp, Vietnam
sights.w: The largest flower-and-ornamental-plant village in the country and the Mekong's Tết-bloom capital — a century-old craft village on the Tiền River raising 2,000+ species across hundreds of hectares, growers tending beds on stilts and by boat. Most photogenic in the weeks before Lunar New Year and during the Sa Đéc flower festival.

sights.n: Làng Nghề Bột Sa Đéc (Sa Đéc Rice-Flour Village)
sights.address: Xã Tân Phú Đông & Phường 2, TP. Sa Đéc, Đồng Tháp, Vietnam
sights.w: The century-old rice-flour craft village strung along the Ngã Bát River whose exceptionally white, fine, non-sour flour is the reason hủ tiếu Sa Đéc tastes the way it does — supplying noodle and cake makers across the south. A working glimpse of the delta's food supply chain behind the region's famous noodles.

sights.n: Làng Gạch Gốm Mang Thít (Mang Thít Brick & Pottery Kilns)
sights.address: Huyện Mang Thít, Vĩnh Long, Vietnam
sights.w: Vĩnh Long's 'Kingdom of Red Kilns' — a 200-year brick-tile-and-pottery landscape of domed beehive kilns clustered along the Thầy Cai canal to the Cổ Chiên River. Once the delta's biggest brick centre with 3,000+ kilns, now around 800 survive and are being conserved as a 'contemporary heritage' site; the weathered red domes make it one of the delta's most striking places to wander and shoot.

sights.n: Nhà Cổ Bình Thủy (Bình Thủy Ancient House)
sights.address: 142-144 Bùi Hữu Nghĩa, P. Bình Thủy, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
sights.w: The finest ancient house in Cần Thơ — the Dương family's five-chamber mansion, first built 1870 and completed in its current Indochine form by 1911, fusing French and Vietnamese-Chinese detail with imported European tiles and ironwork. A national architectural-historical relic (2009) and a film set (it appeared in 'The Lover').

sights.n: Chùa Ông Cần Thơ (Quảng Triệu Hội Quán)
sights.address: 32 Hai Bà Trưng, Ninh Kiều, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
sights.w: A vivid Cantonese assembly hall on the Hậu-River waterfront by Ninh Kiều, built 1894–1896 by Guangdong migrants from Guangzhou and Zhaoqing and dedicated to Quan Cong. Ranked a national historical-architectural relic in 1993, its coiled-dragon roof, incense spirals and red-and-gold interior make it central Cần Thơ's most atmospheric temple.

sights.address: Quốc lộ 1, nối Cần Thơ với Vĩnh Long (sông Hậu), Cần Thơ, Vietnam
sights.w: The great cable-stayed bridge over the Hậu River linking Cần Thơ to Vĩnh Long. On completion in 2010 its 550 m main span was the longest of any cable-stayed bridge in Southeast Asia, ending generations of ferry crossings on National Highway 1 into the western delta — a landmark best seen lit at night from Ninh Kiều.

sights.n: Cồn Sơn (Con Son Island Community Tourism)
sights.address: P. Bùi Hữu Nghĩa, quận Bình Thủy, Cồn Sơn, Cần Thơ, Vietnam
sights.w: A 70-ha orchard islet mid-Hậu-River where ~30 farming households run a genuine community-tourism cooperative: visit floating fish rafts, make folk cakes with local families, pick fruit, and watch the famous 'flying snakehead fish' leap in formation to be fed. A slower, hands-on alternative to the standard floating-market run, reached by short boat hop from Bình Thủy.
